Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

PhysioOpenSim 0.1.2

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a non-portable assertion in the OpenSim parity test (test-opensim-parity.R) that broke the Windows binary builds. The setup writer normalizes output paths via normalizePath(mustWork = FALSE), which leaves a non-existent relative path unchanged on Linux/macOS but absolutizes it on Windows; the test now matches the <output_gen_force_file> tag by basename so it passes on all platforms. No change to package behaviour.

PhysioOpenSim 0.1.1

Validation

  • Added an OpenSim parity fixture and test (VAL-06). PhysioOpenSim is a thin wrapper whose native model parser and CLI tools require an OpenSim-enabled build, so a fully OpenSim-free numeric parity is impossible; the new always-running check validates the pure-R setup writer against real OpenSim: OpenSim’s InverseDynamicsTool loads a PhysioOpenSim-generated ID setup and reads its numeric fields (time_range, lowpass) back exactly (recorded in the bundled reference). A bundled real model (inst/extdata/arm26.osim, from opensim-models) plus its OpenSim summary now back the native-parser parity on OpenSim-enabled builds, replacing the PHYSIO_OPENSIM_MODEL env var. Generated by data-raw/opensim_reference.{R,py} (OpenSim 4.6).

PhysioOpenSim 0.1.0

Initial release as a standalone package in the x-biosignal (PhysioExperiment) ecosystem. PhysioOpenSim provides a native OpenSim C++ bridge for R via Rcpp, exposing model-level operations and full-tool execution to support biomechanics workflows. OpenSim linkage is optional at build time; when OpenSim is not detected, the package still installs and OpenSim-dependent calls fail with informative runtime errors.

New Features

  • Build and availability introspection so downstream code can adapt to the local environment:
    • opensimAvailable() reports whether the package was compiled with OpenSim headers and libraries linked, and opensimBuildConfig() returns the detection method and compilation status.
    • opensimCLIPath() resolves the opensim-cmd executable (via the argument, the OPENSIM_CLI environment variable, or PATH) and opensimCLIAvailable() checks resolvability without raising an error.
  • Native OpenSim model handles backed by C++ external pointers:
    • opensimLoadModel() loads an .osim model into a PhysioOpenSimModel handle, with opensimModelInitialize() and opensimModelIsInitialized() managing the system state.
    • opensimModelSummary() returns structural metadata (body, joint, marker, muscle, and coordinate counts plus total mass) from a file path or a loaded handle, and opensimModelComponents() lists the corresponding component names.
    • opensimModelName(), opensimSetModelName(), opensimFinalizeConnections(), and opensimSaveModel() inspect, rename, finalize connections on, and serialize a model back to XML.
  • Tool execution with a dual native/CLI backend selected via the execution argument ("auto", "native", or "cli"):
    • opensimRunTool() runs any tool setup XML, returning a structured result with execution mode, status, captured stdout/stderr, and elapsed time, and supporting a working directory, extra CLI arguments, a timeout, and optional fail-on-error.
    • Tool-specific wrappers opensimRunIK(), opensimRunID(), opensimRunSO(), opensimRunAnalyze(), opensimRunCMC(), and opensimRunRRA() cover inverse kinematics, inverse dynamics, static optimization, analysis, computed muscle control, and the residual reduction algorithm.
  • Setup XML templating that fills tag values in an existing OpenSim template:
    • opensimWriteToolSetupFromTemplate() performs tag replacement with strict or permissive handling of missing tags and reports applied and missing tags.
    • Convenience wrappers opensimWriteIKSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteIDSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteSOSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteAnalyzeSetupFromTemplate(), opensimWriteRRASetupFromTemplate(), and opensimWriteCMCSetupFromTemplate() normalize model, motion, marker, and loads paths and accept an optional time range and results directory for each tool.
